rules.message: Structural directives are the old control flow. The built-in blocks need no import, type-narrow, and require a track expression.
rules.fix: Use @if, @for (x of xs; track x.id), and @switch. Run the control flow migration only when the task asks for it.

rules.message: track $index ties the DOM and its state to the position. After a delete or a sort, focus, input values, and selection move to the wrong row.
rules.fix: Track a stable id: @for (row of rows(); track row.id). $index is fine only for a list that never changes.

rules.fix: Use a field: private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);

rules.message: The eager strategy checks the component on each change in the app and depends on zone.js. OnPush is the default in Angular 22.
rules.fix: Remove the line (Angular 22) or use ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush (Angular 21), and update the state with signals.

rules.message: In Angular 22, HttpClient uses Fetch by default and withFetch() is deprecated. In Angular 21, withFetch() is correct: suppress the finding with that reason.
rules.fix: Angular 22: provideHttpClient(). Use withXhr() only for upload progress.
Use provideHttpClient() and, in tests, provideHttpClientTesting() after it.

rules.message: A button that is disabled while the form is invalid gives no reason, and a keyboard user cannot reach it (WCAG 3.3.1).
rules.fix: Keep the button enabled. On submit, show all errors and move the focus to the first field with an error. Disable it only while the request runs: [disabled]="submitting()".

rules.message: The date part of toISOString() is the UTC date. For a local midnight in a time zone east of UTC it is the day before.
rules.fix: Build yyyy-MM-dd from getFullYear(), getMonth() + 1, and getDate(), or send the value of <input type="date"> as it is.
